printed_headline_estimate: Chi-square / Cramer's V tests across 6 satisfaction/perception items (n = 448): Gender (Cramer's V = 0.279 to 0.855, P < 0.001, Table 5, PDF p. 10), Age (Cramer's V = 0.262 to 0.688, P < 0.001, Table 6, PDF pp. 11-12), Municipality (Cramer's V = 0.257 to 0.702, P < 0.001, Table 7, PDF p. 14), and Physical Water Source (Cramer's V = 0.357 to 0.801, P < 0.001, Table 8, PDF p. 16).
publication_year_note: Published in African Journal of Governance and Development, Volume 11, Issue 1.2, November 2022 (pp. 256-275; DOI: 10.36369/2616-9045/2022/v11si2a3); no separate online-first year is printed.
rationale: The full text reports inferential statistics (Chi-square tests and Cramer's V with P < 0.001 on n = 448 households in Tables 5-8), alongside descriptive statistics on water supply and borehole/tanker functionality (Tables 1-4). However, the tested independent variables are strictly respondent gender (Table 5), respondent age (Table 6), unordered rural municipality name within Vhembe District Municipality (Table 7, Collins Chabane, Makhado, Musina, Thulamela, where variation is attributed to reliance on groundwater vs. piped surface water), and physical water source type (Table 8, borehole, dam tap, river, springs/wells, water tanker). None of the inferential tests evaluates a narrow rule-type legal, tenure, tariff, administrative discretion, enforcement, ownership, or governance exposure against a service access outcome, and 'effectiveness of community participation' is analyzed only as a subjective perception outcome across those four predictors rather than as an explanatory intervention variable. Thus, no SWiM-eligible effect is reported.
